solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It protects one against a fall

definitions.text: It protects one against a fall

parts.words: It protects one against a fall
parts.note: a fall here is a fall of rain, not a tumble, so the protector is the thing held overhead in a shower

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests a stumble or a drop from height; read it as a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is carried overhead precisely to shield the holder from rainfall.

clue.text: Blustering martinet drops in for material

indicators.note: blustering is wild and stormy, so the letters of the officer are whipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram pool
taken as written: these two letters are what the pool loses

explanation.surface: A bullying disciplinarian stops by and starts throwing his weight around about the cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' tells you to take IN out of MARTINET, leaving MARTET, which 'Blustering' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter and material are synonyms for the stuff a thing is made of.

clue.text: Drink's plonked on bar — short — in a Havana 6 down

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on top of another comes first

parts.note: rum is a drink; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the last letter of bar goes

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A glass of spirit is banged down on a bar counter in a Cuban dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 down is DANCE, so the definition is a Cuban dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance that originated in Cuba, whose capital is Havana.

clue.text: Boozer on other side limited to one place

parts.note: in Britain a boozer is a pub, and your nearest one is your local

indicators.note: other suggests a different version of the word side, here its letters in a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pub across the road has a licence restricted to a single site.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is the British term for your regular neighbourhood pub; 'on' just joins it to the rearranged SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something localised is confined or restricted to one particular area.

clue.text: Medicine made from insect venom?

parts.note: an ant is an insect
ants sting with formic acid, so their venom is an acid

explanation.surface: A remedy concocted from the poison of a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'venom' reading is a playful pun on the remedy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid is a medicine taken to neutralise stomach acid and relieve indigestion.

clue.text: Bird that's big at the fair

definitions.meaning: a bird of fast-flowing streams that bobs and dives for food

explanation.surface: A bird that is a hit at the funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a small diving songbird and, with 'big', to a rollercoaster ride.

clue.text: Trip over the floor perhaps

parts.note: trip suggests stumbling, but to trip is also to step lightly, as when moving across a ballroom floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip over' looks like a fall; read 'trip' as a light step and 'floor' as the dancefloor.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip the light fantastic is to step nimbly across the floor to music.

clue.text: Maybe Harry put on weight in college in America

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: Harry, son of King Charles, is an example of a prince
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A royal gains a few pounds while studying at a university in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that Harry is just one example of a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is a leading Ivy League university in New Jersey.

clue.text: First lady starts reordering extra unendingly

parts.note: in the Bible Eve is the first woman

indicators.note: the start of the word reordering supplies its opening letter

parts.note: extra means more

explanation.surface: A president's wife begins rearranging the spare items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' looks like a president's wife but means the first woman, Eve; 'reordering' is not an anagram signal but only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore is an old adverb meaning always or for all time.

clue.text: Cat, one in a hundred, shows this kind of energy

indicators.note: in tells us cat and one go inside the other pieces

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a tom is a male cat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rare cat in a hundred shows great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in a hundred' looks like a rarity; in fact TOM and I go between A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic energy is power released from the nuclei of atoms.

clue.text: One under-employed in Cornwall

parts.note: under-employed suggests lacking work, but here it means employed underground, digging in the Cornish mines for a metal

explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall, a county in south-west England, was famous for its tin mines; 'under-employed' means working below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornish workers dug tin ore from deep underground shafts for centuries.

clue.text: Harsh-sounding climate left burning

indicators.note: burning suggests letters melted and reshaped, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A scorching climate with nobody remaining sounds grating.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallic sound is harsh and clanging, like metal struck on metal.

clue.text: What pitchers do in a field

definitions.text: What pitchers do in a field

parts.words: What pitchers do in a field
parts.note: pitchers suggests baseball players, but here they are campers who pitch tents in a meadow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitchers' and 'field' suggest baseball or cricket; think instead of people pitching tents.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up a camp, which is what people pitching tents in a meadow do.

clue.text: On motorway, deplorable 'undertaking' leads to accidental killing

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI
sad can mean pitiful or deplorable
a venture is an undertaking or enterprise

explanation.surface: A dreadful job on the motorway results in a fatal crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I. 'Undertaking' in quotes hints at an undertaker but means a venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Death by misadventure is the British inquest verdict for an accidental death.

clue.text: Duck near germs spreading

indicators.note: germs spreading suggests infection, but it tells us the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A water bird is close to an outbreak of infection.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating diving duck with a serrated bill.

clue.text: Being in Exodus, briefly, first in this French translation

parts.note: Ex is the standard short form of the book of Exodus
first can be written 1st, read as IST
translated into French, in is en and this is ce

explanation.surface: A creature appears in the Bible's second book, in a new French version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' tells you to put 'in this' into French: EN and CE. 'first' is written 1st, with the numeral read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being and existence both mean the state of being alive or real.

clue.text: Email son ingredients for pudding

indicators.note: ingredients are separate parts mixed together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Send your boy the recipe for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina boiled with milk and sugar is a classic British milk pudding.

clue.text: Mill round copier, working in time for copy

indicators.note: working in means fitting something into the middle of another thing
to mill is to grind up, so the letters are crushed and remixed

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A machine shop goes round the photocopier, getting it running in time to make a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mill' and 'round' both look like machinery, but only 'Mill' signals the rearrangement; 'working in' then tucks the time letter into the scrambled result before the final two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproduction is a copy of something such as a painting or piece of furniture.

clue.text: Warm drink? Not usually

parts.note: warm means friendly, and a fruit squash is a drink that is not usually served hot

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a hot drink; in fact one word means both warm (friendly) and a drink usually served cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly, and is also a sweet fruit drink diluted with cold water.

clue.text: Theologian in the distance is halfway

indicators.note: in tells us the theologian sits inside the distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree, standing for a theologian

explanation.surface: A churchman far away is midway along.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at the middle point is halfway between two ends.

clue.text: Gold in large quantity seen in marsh

indicators.note: in places gold inside the large quantity

parts.note: a mass is a large quantity
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Lots of gold is spotted in a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a boggy area of wet ground, a marsh or swamp.

clue.text: Bony nutcase

parts.note: nutcase suggests a lunatic, but read as a case for the nut, the head, made of bone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' is slang for the head, so a bony case for it is the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony framework enclosing the brain is the casing of the head.

clue.text: Lock of hair — the last one sees of vermin?

parts.note: rats are vermin
the last part of an animal you see as it runs off is its tail

explanation.surface: A wisp of hair is all you glimpse of a fleeing rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: A rat's tail is a thin lock of hair, often worn at the nape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat's tail is a long thin strand or lock of hair resembling a rodent's tail.

clue.text: Story book to be imported by board

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so book is brought into story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A novel is brought in by a company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a company board but defines a flat table.
explanation.definitionFit: Board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board.

clue.text: Girl, our one, in a state

parts.note: miss is a word for a girl
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Our daughter is in a bit of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' suggests being upset; read it as an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is a state in the Midwest of the USA.

clue.text: Nonentity's murder alibi?

definitions.meaning: a nonentity is a person of no importance; the 's stands for 'is'
a murder suspect's best defence is that there is no corpse

explanation.surface: An insignificant person has a defence against a killing charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is an unimportant person, and 'no body' is the plea that no victim was found.

clue.text: Disbar relative clutching drum

indicators.note: clutching means the outer words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A lawyer struck off grips a relation's drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is a cylindrical container, like a barrel.

clue.text: Vassals, fellows from Belgian city

parts.note: Liège is a city in eastern Belgium
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Feudal servants and their companions come from a city in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Liegemen were feudal vassals bound to serve their lord.
